newsitem.title: USA: Canadian domestic spot natgas up on colder weather.
newsitem.headline: Canadian domestic spot natgas up on colder weather.

text.p: Canadian domestic spot natural gas prices edged higher again Friday as colder air moved into the West and the pace of storage withdrawals escalated, market sources said.
At the AECO storage hub, prices for the weekend gained more than five cents to the C$1.65-1.67 per gigajoule (GJ) area, down about $1 from February's indices.
Temperatures in Calgary are forecast to hover below normal through at least early next week, with a low of about -15 degrees Celsius expected on Sunday, traders said.
"There was also about 900 (million cubic feet per day) of gas taken out of storage yesterday," one trader said, noting the larger-than-expected drawdown also helped to boost prices.

At Sumas, Wash, most deals were confirmed done in the $1.23-1.25 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) range. This matches Thursday's late morning daily prices when news surfaced that Westcoast Energy would be cutting about 25 percent of production, or about 170 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd), at its McMahon gas plant in B.C.
Most likely keeping a lid on Sumas prices was news that Westcoast Energy's McMahon gas plant would be back to full capacity on Saturday after a series of snags. All constraints will be lifted.
However, the company said the force majeure remains in effect so that operators can do additional testing to better determine the root of the problem.
At Niagara, prices for the weekend were mostly steady in the $2.07-2.12 per mmBtu area in sparse trade, falling about $1.30 under February indices.
